name: Stade de France
notes: RER B (La Plaine) + RER D (Stade de France) + M13/T8 (Porte de Paris) + M14 (Pleyel, from 2024). ZDC 490784 is absent from validations before 2024 because M14 did not reach Pleyel until then.

name: Parc des Princes
notes: M9 and M10. Shares its catchment with Stade Jean-Bouin, 400m away -- attribute event days carefully when both are in use.

name: Plenitude Arena (ex Paris La Defense Arena)
notes: Renamed Plenitude Arena in 2025. La Defense (71517) is a six-line interchange, so its baseline dwarfs the event signal; Nanterre-Prefecture and Nanterre-La-Folie are the cleaner indicators.

name: Accor Arena
notes: Gare de Bercy is 174m away. Gare de Lyon (73626) is a mainline terminus and will not show an event signal above its own baseline.

name: Stade Roland-Garros
notes: Attendance is spread across courts and across a two-week tournament rather than concentrated in one session, so the daily profile differs fundamentally from a stadium event.

name: Stade Jean-Bouin
notes: Catchment overlaps Parc des Princes almost entirely.

name: Adidas Arena
notes: Opened February 2024, so there is no pre-2024 history to learn from.

name: Zenith Paris - La Villette
notes: Sits inside Parc de la Villette; the Philharmonie and Grande Halle draw on the same stations.

name: Stade Sebastien Charlety
notes: T3a stop is 75m from the ground. Cite universitaire (70623) carries a large student baseline.

name: Paris Expo Porte de Versailles
notes: Porte de Versailles (71045) is 21m away and is the dominant signal. Trade fairs run multi-day, so the shape is a plateau rather than a spike.

name: Parc des Expositions de Paris-Nord Villepinte
notes: Served by a single dedicated RER B station (Parc des Expositions), which makes it the cleanest trade-fair signal in the region.

name: La Seine Musicale
notes: On Ile Seguin. T2 Brimborion is nearest at 152m but low-capacity; Pont de Sevres (M9) carries most of the load.
